qualitative.gate_2_reason: Non-essential, deferrable overflow storage service; discretionary consumer spending vulnerable to moves, decluttering, and economic belt-tightening.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 2 (Rejected – G2 Essential Need). Public Storage provides self-storage rentals, which represent a discretionary and deferrable convenience rather than an essential functional necessity or entrenched everyday habit. Units store non-essential household overflow and clutter, making contracts easily cancellable during economic strain or housing freezes. Furthermore, capital-intensive real estate asset intensity results in multi-year ROIC of ~7-8%, failing quality compounding hurdles.
qualitative.evidence: Public Storage (PSA) operates ~3,000 self-storage properties across the US with ~218M sq ft. While PSA achieves high property-level NOI margins (>77%) and maintains an A-rated balance sheet, self-storage fails Munger essentiality. Storage space is a deferrable consumer discretionary expense driven by temporary moves and excess clutter. During 2023-2025 post-pandemic normalization and sluggish housing turnover, pricing power on new move-ins contracted. Structurally, capital-intensive real estate ownership caps 10-year median ROIC at ~8.2% (2024-2025 ROIC ~7.2%), far below the >=12% compounding hurdle.
